_note: General, state-dependent topics. Notes must never state a statutory limit, number or conclusion: only that rules differ and who can confirm. Written by the LexLocal team.

security deposit.note: Rules on how large a deposit can be and how and when it must be returned can differ by state and by local tenancy law.

lock-in and early exit.note: How a lock-in period interacts with a tenant's or employee's right to leave early depends on the applicable law and the exact wording.

rent increase.note: Some states regulate how and when rent can be increased under their tenancy laws.

eviction and vacating.note: Eviction and recovery of possession follow state rent-control or tenancy procedures, which differ across India.

registration and stamp duty.note: Stamp duty and registration requirements for leases and licences differ by state. A local lawyer or the sub-registrar office can confirm what applies.

arbitration.note: How an arbitration clause works, including who appoints the arbitrator, depends on the applicable law. A lawyer can explain what it means for you.

post-employment restrictions.note: Whether restrictions that apply after employment ends can be relied on depends on the applicable law and the facts. An employment lawyer can advise.

training bond or repayment.note: Whether an employer can recover training or other costs when an employee leaves depends on the applicable law and the facts.

working hours and leave.note: Working hours, leave and overtime can be covered by state shops-and-establishments rules as well as the contract.

late payment interest.note: How courts treat interest, late fees and penalties can depend on the applicable law and the circumstances.
